thesis: Shahrazad changes the structure of a match by creating a subgame whose result halves a player's remaining life, making time, logistics, and tournament policy as important as ordinary card advantage.

canonicalIdentity.originalPrintedText: Players play a Magic subgame, using their libraries as their decks. Each player who doesn't win the subgame loses half their life, rounded up.

competitiveTimeline.significance: No credible sanctioned tournament archive exists for Shahrazad. The article now labels Groundhog Day and Storytime as curated historical constructions rather than tournament registrations and binds the documented Groundhog Day source.

playbook.role: Use it only under a clearly agreed rules framework and with enough time and space to complete the subgame. In casual Old School, build the subdeck plan so both the main game and subgame advance the same pressure.

counterplay.directAnswers: Counter the spell, pressure the caster's life total so halving is less meaningful, and establish event policy before play. In sanctioned Magic the card is not a normal competitive option, so counterplay is principally relevant to community formats.
